en: Itivuttaka 102 Catukkanipāta Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of gifts. What four? The gift of material things, the gift of Dhamma, the gift of safety, and the gift of loving-kindness. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of gifts. When this was said, a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, what is the difference between one who offers a sacrifice and one who enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice? “There is a case, brahmin, where someone offers a sacrifice, but another enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. This is the first way in which one who offers a sacrifice differs from one who enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. Then again, brahmin, someone else enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice, but another offers a sacrifice. This is the second way... Then again, brahmin, someone else both offers a sacrifice and enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. This is the third way... Then again, brahmin, someone else neither offers a sacrifice nor enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. This is the fourth way in which one who offers a sacrifice differs from one who enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. [The Blessed One continued: “Brahmin, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The person who offers a sacrifice but does not enjoy the fruit of that sacrifice; the person who enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice but does not offer a sacrifice; the person who both offers a sacrifice and enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice; and the person who neither offers a sacrifice nor enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. And how, brahmin, is one a person who offers a sacrifice but does not enjoy the fruit of that sacrifice? Here, brahmin, someone offers a sacrifice, thinking: ‘May this gift of mine go to my mother and father. Having offered the sacrifice, he goes to a bad destination, to hell. His mother and father, on the other hand, enjoy the fruit of that sacrifice. It is in this way that one is a person who offers a sacrifice but does not enjoy the fruit of that sacrifice. And how, brahmin, is one a person who enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice but does not offer a sacrifice? Here, brahmin, someone enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice, thinking: ‘May this gift of mine go to my mother and father. But his mother and father do not enjoy the fruit of that sacrifice. It is in this way that one is a person who enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice but does not offer a sacrifice. And how, brahmin, is one a person who both offers a sacrifice and enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice? Here, brahmin, someone offers a sacrifice, thinking: ‘May this gift of mine go to my mother and father. Having offered the sacrifice, he goes to a good destination, to a heavenly world. His mother and father also enjoy the fruit of that sacrifice. It is in this way that one is a person who both offers a sacrifice and enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. And how, brahmin, is one a person who neither offers a sacrifice nor enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice? Here, brahmin, someone neither offers a sacrifice nor enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice. It is in this way that one is a person who neither offers a sacrifice nor enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice. These, brahmin, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The brahmin said: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! Just as if one were to set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has Master Gotama explained the Dhamma in various ways. I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life shall last. “Brahmin, one who offers a sacrifice is rare indeed; one who enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice is rare indeed; one who both offers a sacrifice and enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice is rare indeed. But one who neither offers a sacrifice nor enjoys the fruit of that sacrifice is very rare. [The brahmin said: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama!

The Discourse on the Destruction of the Taints.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know and does not see."
And what, monks, does one know, what does one see, for the destruction of the taints to occur?
Monks, for one who knows and sees, "This is suffering," the destruction of the taints occurs.

Monks, for one who knows and sees, "This is the origin of suffering," the destruction of the taints occurs. Monks, for one who knows and sees, "This is the cessation of suffering," [the destruction of the taints occurs].
“Monks, for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
Monks, it is for one who knows thus and sees thus that the destruction of the taints occurs.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“For one in training, who is still practicing the training...”
Following the straight path,
there is first the knowledge of destruction,
and immediately thereafter, full penetration.
Then, for one liberated by final knowledge,
the supreme knowledge of liberation arises— the knowledge of destruction.
"The fetters are destroyed"—
this is not [attained] by one who is indolent,
foolish, and lacking in understanding.
“Nibbāna is to be realized, the liberation from all fetters.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The third.
